answer: Rotating kernel challenge. Each identity must solve a fresh, instance-specific puzzle derived from a hidden kernel seeded per epoch; solutions cannot be copied because the kernel rotates before reuse. An attacker cloning identities must pay full compute per clone each epoch, since cached answers fail at the ridge between epochs. Registration also requires submitting a valid orchard-tagged proof tied to live state, so precomputed pools expire. Cost scales linearly with clone count times epoch frequency, making sustained sybil farming economically unviable.
